text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> page fired: PD-2312 svc-infer-west2: GPU OOM rate spike (72/min). Primary symptoms: nvml out-of-memory, cublas allocation failures. Affected pool: infer-west2a-pool. Links: https://pagerduty.example/PD-2312 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Event details attached. Escalation policy: oncall-sre -> infra -> eng-ml. Auto-retries suppressed.

alice_oncall: Acked PD-2312. I'm on it. Pulling logs from the pool and checking recent deploys.

bob_infra: Seeing correlated evictions on nodes gpu-24..gpu-27. Kernel logs show repeated "CUDA allocation failed" and "nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo error".

charlie_sre: Any recent model rollouts or batch config changes? Could be a hot prefix/long-seq workload.

kevin_ml: No deploys in the last 6h. We did enable a temporary higher-seq test job earlier today but it should be isolated to staging. I'll check job history.

maria_support: Customer A reported increased 503s ~ 10:12 UTC. They saw degraded latency on chat endpoints.

alice_oncall: Noted customer impact. Setting severity to SEV2 until we know scope and restore path. Starting mitigations: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) reroute traffic off infer-west2a to west2b, 3) lower per-request max_seq on hosted plan to 1024.

bob_infra: Running command to cordon nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-24 gpu-25 gpu-26 gpu-27 -n inference`

bob_infra: Rerouting policy update: applying temporary route rule to prefer infer-west2b for model: `model:open-llama-13b` TTL=15m.

alice_oncall: Applying per-route rate-limit tweak via console UI, will post screenshots. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

charlie_sre: Quick check: GPU memory fragmentation looks high on those nodes (free blocks small). NVML traces attached: ```
E: 2026-03-17T10:12:22Z nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo failed: out of memory
E: 2026-03-17T10:12:23Z cublasCreate returned error 3
```

kevin_ml: Suggest switching inference fallback to quantized 4-bit variant to reduce per-request memory footprint while we rebuild capacity. Can we enable model-fallback policy?

alice_oncall: Enabling fallback to q4/llama-13b-fq for hosted tier. Triggered rollout. Noting potential quality delta.

maria_support: Alerting Customer A that we've routed traffic and are enabling a temporary fallback; message drafted for status page.

bob_infra: Evicted pods on the four nodes, starting drain. Running `kubectl drain gpu-24 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference` now.

charlie_sre: After drain, telemetry shows OOM rate dropping to 8/min and error 503s falling. CPU usage on west2b increased but within limits.

alice_oncall: Good. Keeping PD-2312 open until full stabilization and root cause. Next: collect heap dumps from affected pods, capture kernel oops if any, and coordinate with hardware vendor if needed.

kevin_ml: I'll run an eval on fallback model prompt set to quantify quality regression; post results in 15m.

maria_support: Posting to status page: "We experienced a GPU memory pressure event in west2a affecting model inference throughput. Traffic was rerouted and temporary fallback models enabled. Mitigation in progress."

pagerduty: PD-2312: Alert acknowledgements: alice_oncall. Escalation stopped.

alice_oncall: Handoff to bob_infra for extended investigation and charlie_sre for postmortem. I'll remain available for customer comms.

bob_infra: Logged follow-up ticket INFRA-4487 with node diagnostics and nvml traces. Will coordinate hardware checks.

charlie_sre: Captured timeline and will start a blameless postmortem doc. Tentative RCA hypotheses: 1) memory fragmentation due to long-lived KV cache growth, 2) a pathological user request pattern causing large KV cache entries, 3) possible CUDA driver bug under sustained small-alloc churn.

alice_oncall: Closing mitigation loop: nodes drained, traffic rerouted, fallback enabled, customer notified. Marking incident as "mitigated" in PD but keep open for RCA.

maria_support: Customer A confirmed degraded latency reduced after the reroute. They appreciate the quick update.

alice_oncall: Thanks team. I'll create a calendar follow-up for runbook improvements and export telemetry to support the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
